name: cadillac_v16_452
label: Cadillac V-16 7.4 L (Series 452, 1930)

sources.what: Hagerty feature 'Sweet V-16: Cadillac's most exotic engine' by Don Sherman, built on William Strickland's 1930 engineering paper; the best technical account I could open.
English Wikipedia Cadillac V16 engine page; infobox figures citing period sources.

notes: Sourced: bore, stroke, 5.5:1 compression, 45-degree V-16 on an eight-throw crank (the two rods of each pair share a pin), even 45-degree firing, one intake and one exhaust valve per cylinder, one carburettor and one log manifold per bank, dual exhaust pipes, 165 hp at 3400 rpm and 320 lb-ft at 1400 rpm. The firing ORDER and cylinder numbering were not found and are assumed: each bank fires in a common straight-eight order (1-6-2-5-8-3-7-4, on throws 90 degrees apart like a straight-eight's) with the other bank's cylinder on the same pin following 45 degrees later. Estimated, not sourced: rod length, valve diameters and lifts, cam timing (mild, as for a quiet 1930 engine), manifold runner, carburettor and exhaust sizes, a long silencer, rev limit (4000 rpm; none was published), idle speed. Tuning ended with friction_scale and heat_q at the ends of their allowed ranges (1.2 and 2.2e6), which is how the model was brought down to this engine's low output; a real 1930 engine also loses charge to its heated intake manifold, which the simulator does not model. The two carburettors and two intake manifolds are entered as one plenum with one throttle. Left to the simulator's defaults: plenum and airbox, collector volume, flywheel inertia. Also estimates: friction_scale, heat_q, burn_scale (the simulator's friction, heat-release and burn-rate scales), set with the other estimated fields so that simulated torque and power come near the published figures; no sourced number was changed.

vehicle.name: Cadillac V-16 Fleetwood Imperial sedan, style 4375 (1930)
vehicle.notes: Three-speed synchromesh manual; its gear ratios were not found, so gears are left to the simulator. Final drive is the standard 4.39 (4.07 and 4.75 optional). Style 4375, the seven-passenger Imperial sedan, was the second most built V-16 body; the most built, the five-passenger 4375-S, has no published weight. The 6,020 lb weight is from a reference listing that does not say whether it is shipping or curb weight. Tyres were 7.00-19 early in the year and 7.50-19 from mid-year. wheel_radius_m and top speed omitted (only a range, 80 to 100 mph by body, was found).
